name: Dandruff Prone Scalp
description: A scalp condition characterized by flaking skin and visible dandruff, which can be caused by various factors including dryness, oiliness, or underlying medical conditions.
common_problems: Visible flakes in hair and on clothes
recommended_product_categories: Shampoos and conditioners designed for dandruff
washing_frequency: Twice a week, or as directed by a dermatologist

morning_routine.action: Wash your hair with an anti-dandruff shampoo.
morning_routine.purpose: Remove dandruff and prevent further flaking.

night_routine.action: Rinse thoroughly to remove all traces of the shampoo.
night_routine.purpose: Ensure no residue remains, which could cause irritation.

weekly_care: Apply a leave-in anti-dandruff treatment if recommended by your dermatologist.
deep_conditioning_frequency: Once a month or as needed
heat_styling_recommendation: Minimize heat styling, and use heat protectants when necessary.
lifestyle_tips: Use gentle hair care products without harsh chemicals
common_mistakes: Using products that do not address dandruff
Ignoring symptoms and not seeking professional advice
do: Follow a consistent skincare routine as recommended by your dermatologist
Stay hydrated to help manage dryness
Consider using natural oils like tea tree oil for mild relief (consult with a dermatologist before use)
dont: Scratch the scalp, which can irritate and worsen dandruff
Use overly strong or irritating products
Assume that all flakes are due to dandruff; consult a professional if unsure

seasonal_care.summer: Stay hydrated and use gentle hair care products to prevent dryness.
seasonal_care.winter: Moisturize regularly, as cold weather can strip the scalp of natural oils.
seasonal_care.monsoon: Protect your scalp from excessive moisture, which can lead to fungal growth.

expert_tips: Regular follow-ups with a dermatologist are essential for managing dandruff.
Use a scalp massager during your routine to improve circulation and promote healthier skin.
